questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Center of a Vertical Hyperbola
questions.problem: What is the center of the hyperbola $\frac{(y-5)^{2}}{36}-\frac{(x+1)^{2}}{4}=1?$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

Note that the given equation can be rewritten as follows:

$$
\frac{(y-5)^{2}}{{6}^{2}}-\frac{(x-(-1))^{2}}{{2}^{2}}=1
$$

In this case, we have $h=-1$ and $k=5.$

Therefore, the center of the hyperbola is $(-1,5).$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Center of a Horizontal Hyperbola Given an Equation in Expanded Form
questions.problem:
What is the center of the hyperbola 
$6{x}^{2}-4{y}^{2}+48x-48y=72?$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}6{x}^{2}-4{y}^{2}+48x-48y & =72 \\ 6{x}^{2}+48x-4{y}^{2}-48y & =72 \\ 6[{x}^{2}+8x]-4[{y}^{2}+12y] & =72 \\ 6[(x+4)^{2}-16]-4[(y+6)^{2}-36] & =72 \\ 6(x+4)^{2}-96-4(y+6)^{2}+144 & =72 \\ 6(x+4)^{2}-4(y+6)^{2} & =24 \\ \frac{(x+4)^{2}}{4}-\frac{(y+6)^{2}}{6} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-(-4))^{2}}{{2}^{2}}-\frac{(y-(-6))^{2}}{(\sqrt{6})^{2}} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the center is $(-4,-6).$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Center of a Vertical Hyperbola Given an Equation in Expanded Form
questions.problem: What is the center of the hyperbola $6{y}^{2}-4{x}^{2}-60y+8x=-122?$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}6{y}^{2}-4{x}^{2}-60y+8x & =-122 \\ 6{y}^{2}-60y-4{x}^{2}+8x & =-122 \\ 6[{y}^{2}-10y]-4[{x}^{2}-2x] & =-122 \\ 6[(y-5)^{2}-25]-4[(x-1)^{2}-1] & =-122 \\ 6(y-5)^{2}-150-4(x-1)^{2}+4 & =-122 \\ 6(y-5)^{2}-4(x-1)^{2} & =-122+150-4 \\ 6(y-5)^{2}-4(x-1)^{2} & =24 \\ \frac{(y-5)^{2}}{4}-\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{6} & =1 \\ \frac{(y-5)^{2}}{{2}^{2}}-\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{(\sqrt{6})^{2}} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center is $(1,5).$

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}16{y}^{2}-25{x}^{2}+96y & =256 \\ 16{y}^{2}+96y\,-\,25{x}^{2} & =256 \\ 16[{y}^{2}+6y]\,-\,25{x}^{2} & =256 \\ 16[(y+3)^{2}-9]\,-\,25{x}^{2} & =256 \\ 16(y+3)^{2}-144\,-\,25{x}^{2} & =256 \\ 16(y+3)^{2}-25{x}^{2} & =256+144 \\ 16(y+3)^{2}-25{x}^{2} & =400 \\ \frac{(y+3)^{2}}{25}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{16} & =1 \\ \frac{(y-(-3))^{2}}{25}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{16} & =1\end{aligned}
